contract: sh <script> <scratch_dir> <repo_root>; exit 0 on success. The scratch dir is created fresh per repetition and removed outside the timed region.

families.name: startup_nop
families.description: Empty payload. Isolates the launcher's fixed per-invocation cost: sandbox construction plus teardown, paid once for every command an agent shells out to.

families.name: repo_traversal
families.description: rg --files over the workspace, an rg content search, git status and git diff --stat. The read-heavy path a coding agent walks before it changes anything.

families.name: many_small_files
families.description: Create, stat, read and delete 2000 small files. Concentrates path resolution and metadata operations, which is where a Landlock-style boundary does its work.

families.name: process_spawn
families.description: 200 sequential execve plus reap cycles. Every tool an agent runs pays this once.

families.name: python_pkg_test
families.description: Generate a small Python package, byte-compile it, then discover and run its unittest suite. Interpreter startup, import machinery and test discovery.

families.name: node_pkg_test
families.description: pnpm install of a dependency-free package into a run-local store, then a node test run. Package-manager filesystem churn plus runtime startup.

families.name: rust_cargo_metadata
families.description: cargo metadata --no-deps --offline over the workspace manifest. Manifest parsing and workspace resolution without a compile.

families.name: rust_cargo_check
families.description: cargo check -p aa-core. Real toolchain use. Off by default because a cold run costs minutes and dominates a session; enable with --heavy.

families.name: https_loopback
families.description: 200 sequential HTTPS requests against a TLS server the harness runs on loopback. Measures the socket and TLS cost of confinement, isolated from WAN variance. Whether a backend can express AASM egress policy at all is a compatibility question, not this one.
